title: Series vs. parallel
idea: Series is one path, so the current is the same everywhere. Parallel is side by side, so the voltage is the same across each part.

series.title: Series: same current
lines: There is only one path, so every bit of current goes through both resistors. The current is the same through all of them.
To measure current, the meter has to be in that path too: an ammeter or a multimeter set to current goes in series.
A fuse or circuit breaker also goes in series, in the hot wire only, so all the current passes through it.

parallel.title: Parallel: same voltage
lines: Each resistor connects across the same two points, so each gets the same voltage.
To measure voltage, the meter connects across the part the same way: a voltmeter goes in parallel.

compare.how: In series, in the path, so the current flows through it.
In series with the hot wire only. Not the neutral.
An inductor and a capacitor. In series or in parallel, either one counts.

traps.why: In parallel the voltage is the same, but the current splits between the branches.
In series the current is the same, but the voltage is divided between the parts.
Voltage is measured across a part, so the voltmeter goes in parallel with it.
Current has to flow through the meter, so it goes in series.

traps.wrong: In series with the hot and neutral conductors
traps.why: The fuse or breaker goes in the hot wire only, never the neutral.

traps.wrong: In parallel with the hot conductor only
traps.why: A fuse has to carry the circuit's current to protect it, so it goes in series.
